1	# LOOM portal: interface for agents
2	
3	This page is for an agent (or the developer of one) that needs part of a
4	person's health context to do a task for them. It is the only document an
5	agent needs; it does not have to read LOOM's source.
6	
7	## What LOOM offers
8	
9	LOOM holds one person's health record and hands out **task-scoped,
10	expiring slices** of it. You say what task you are doing; LOOM decides
11	how deep you may see, which fields you get, and for how long.
12	
13	| Tier | What it contains | Field names |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| L0 | raw sensor signal | `raw_signal` |
16	| L1 | readings (here: hourly glucose, mg/dL) | `readings` |
17	| L2 | patterns and alerts derived from readings | `glucose_patterns`, `alerts` |
18	| L3 | plain-language constraints | `constraints` |
19	
20	L0 is the deepest (most revealing), L3 the shallowest. A tier includes the
21	shallower ones: an L2 grant may carry `constraints` too.
22	
23	## Access
24	
25	- Base URL and namespace are given to you by whoever runs the portal (for
26	  a test: `http://127.0.0.1:8787` and a namespace such as `demo`).
27	  Every call for one person goes to `/v1/<namespace>/...`.
28	- There is no login in v0.1. You identify yourself with `agent_id` (this
29	  agent instance) and `publisher` (the company or developer that ships
30	  it). In Nanda Town the gateway fills `agent_id` from the signed envelope;
31	  over plain HTTP both are claims.
32	- JSON in, JSON out. Errors are JSON `{"error": "..."}`.
33	
34	## Endpoints
35	
36	| Method and path | Use |
37	|---|---|
38	| `GET /health` | version and policy id |
39	| `POST /v1/<ns>/requests` | ask for access for a task; a grant carries data immediately |
40	| `POST /v1/<ns>/fetch` | get fresh data again under a grant you already hold |
41	| `GET /v1/<ns>/credit` | publisher → credit score (only publishers that have been seen) |
42	| `GET /v1/<ns>/log` | every decision so far, in order |
43	
44	### `POST /v1/<ns>/requests`: body
45	
46	| Field | Required | Meaning |
47	|---|---|---|
48	| `request_id` | yes | unique per request; reuse it only to retry the same request |
49	| `agent_id` | yes | your agent instance |
50	| `publisher` | yes | who ships you |
51	| `category` | yes | `agent_for_user` (works for the person) or `care_provider` (clinician side) |
52	| `task` | yes | one of the task names below |
53	| `purpose` | no | free text, recorded |
54	| `tier` | yes | the deepest tier you ask for (`L0`..`L3`) |
55	| `fields` | yes | list of field names you ask for |
56	| `at` | yes | current time on the person's timeline, in days (number) |
57	
58	### Tasks (policy `loom-policy-0.1.1`)
59	
60	| `task` | `category` | Deepest tier | Fields you may ask for | Validity |
61	|---|---|---|---|---|
62	| `shopping_list` | `agent_for_user` | L3 | `constraints` | single use |
63	| `meal_plan` | `agent_for_user` | L2 | `glucose_patterns`, `constraints` | 7 days |
64	| `clinical_visit` | `care_provider` | L2 | `glucose_patterns`, `alerts`, `co

input.command:
mkdir -p /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run1/out && cat > /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run1/out/grocer-1.md <<'EOF'
# This week's grocery list (grocer-1, freshcart, day 0)

> **Draft, waiting for your confirmation.** LOOM gave this request `confirmation: first_request`, so please look this over and confirm before anything gets ordered.

Built around two health needs: **limit added sugar** and **prefer low-glycemic foods**. Quantities are for one person for about 7 days.

## Vegetables (non-starchy, eat freely)
- Spinach or mixed salad greens, 2 bags
- Broccoli, 2 heads
- Cauliflower, 1 head
- Zucchini, 3
- Bell peppers, 4 (mixed colours)
- Cucumbers, 2
- Cherry tomatoes, 1 pint
- Green beans, 1 lb
- Onions, 2; garlic, 1 bulb
- Mushrooms, 8 oz
- Frozen mixed vegetables (no sauce), 1 bag

## Fruit (whole, lower-glycemic)
- Berries (blueberries, strawberries or raspberries), 2 pints, or 1 bag frozen unsweetened
- Apples, 4
- Pears, 2
- Oranges or clementines, 4
- Lemons, 2

## Protein
- Eggs, 1 dozen
- Chicken breasts or thighs, 2 lb
- Salmon or other fatty fish, 1 lb (fresh or frozen)
- Canned tuna or sardines in water/olive oil, 2 cans
- Firm tofu, 1 block
- Lentils (dry), 1 lb
- Chickpeas and black beans, 1 can each (low sodium)

## Dairy and alternatives
- Plain unsweetened Greek yogurt, 32 oz
- Cheese (cheddar or feta), 1 block
- Milk or unsweetened soy/almond milk, 1/2 gallon

## Whole grains and starches (low-GI picks, modest portions)
- Steel-cut or rolled oats (plain, not instant flavoured), 1 canister
- Quinoa, 1 lb
- Barley or bulgur, 1 lb
- 100% whole-grain or sprouted bread, 1 loaf
- Sweet potatoes, 2 (in place of white potatoes)

## Nuts, seeds, fats
- Almonds or walnuts (unsalted, unsweetened), 1 bag
- Chia or ground flaxseed, 1 small bag
- Natural peanut or almond butter (no added sugar), 1 jar
- Extra-virgin olive oil (if running low)
- Avocados, 3

## Pantry and flavour
- Canned diced tomatoes, no sugar added, 2 cans
- Low-sodium broth, 1 carton
- Herbs and spices: cinnamon, cumin, paprika, oregano
- Vinegar (apple cider or balsamic) for dressings
- Unsweetened sparkling water or tea

## Skipping this week
Sugary cereals, flavoured/sweetened yogurt, fruit juice, regular soda, white bread, white rice, pastries, candy, granola bars with added sugar, bottled sauces and dressings with added sugar (ketchup, BBQ, teriyaki).

## Shopping tips
- Check labels for "added sugars" on the Nutrition Facts panel; aim for 0 g on sauces, yogurt, bread and nut butters.
- Pair carbs (fruit, oats, bread) with protein or fat to soften their effect.
- Choose intact or less-processed grains (steel-cut oats, barley) over finely milled ones.

This list is general guidance from your stated constraints, not medical advice. If you take glucose-lowering medication or follow a clinician's plan, that plan comes first.

## What I got from LOOM and how I used it
- **Request:** task `shopping_list`, category `agent_for_user`, tier `L3`, field `constraints` only, at day 0. That's exactly what the policy allows for this task, so no overreach.
- **Decision:** `granted` (grant `g-22ecac0724`), single use, validity 0 days. freshcart's credit went 60 → 61. Friction band medium, `confirmation: first_request`.
- **Data received:** `constraints = ["limit_added_sugar", "prefer_low_glycemic"]`. No readings, glucose patterns or alerts (those aren't available to a shopping-list task, and I didn't ask).
- **How I used it:** `limit_added_sugar` drove the "skipping" section, the unsweetened/no-sugar-added product choices and the label tip. `prefer_low_glycemic` drove the emphasis on non-starchy vegetables, legumes, intact whole grains, sweet potato over white potato, whole fruit over juice, and protein/fat pairings.
- **Confirmation:** because the grant asks for confirmation on first request, this list is a draft for you to approve before ordering.
- **Retention:** the grant was single use; I made no further fetches and keep nothing beyond this file.
EOF

input.message: I made this week's grocery list and saved it to /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run1/out/grocer-1.md. I read only AGENT_INTERFACE.md and then made one request to the LOOM portal (namespace coldstart-1, day 0) as agent `grocer-1`, publisher `freshcart`. The request was task `shopping_list`, category `agent_for_user`, tier `L3`, field `constraints` only, which is exactly what the policy allows for this task. It was granted (grant `g-22ecac0724`, single use, valid for 0 days), and freshcart's credit went from 60 to 61. The only data returned were two constraints: `limit_added_sugar` and `prefer_low_glycemic`. No readings, glucose patterns or alerts were asked for or received. The list is for one person for about a week, sorted by store section: non-starchy vegetables, whole lower-glycemic fruit, lean proteins and legumes, plain unsweetened dairy, intact whole grains and sweet potatoes, nuts and seeds, and no-sugar-added pantry items. It also has a "skipping this week" section (juice, soda, sweetened yogurt and cereal, white bread and rice, sugary sauces), tips on reading labels and pairing carbs with protein or fat, and a note that it isn't medical advice. LOOM returned `confirmation: first_request`, so the list is marked as a draft the user needs to confirm before anything is ordered. I didn't call fetch again because the grant was single use. The file ends with the required "What I got from LOOM and how I used it" section.
